title: Implement Cognito CLI authentication and dashboard client support
description:
Purpose: Implement the official human authentication path.

Owned scope:
- Cognito hosted authorization configuration required for authorization-code PKCE.
- plexus login, plexus whoami, and plexus logout.
- Operating-system keychain credential storage and automatic refresh.
- Explicit Cognito bearer-token transport in PlexusDashboardClient while retaining explicit IAM workload authentication.

Exclusions:
- Artifact ticket resolver and storage-consumer migrations.
- AWS SSO, public API-key, or automatic authentication fallbacks.

Acceptance:
- Behavior-first tests cover login, loopback callback validation, PKCE, keychain persistence, refresh, whoami, logout, revoked sessions, and explicit auth modes.
- Protected commands fail with plexus login guidance when application authentication is unavailable.
- Existing workload IAM behavior remains supported.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Kickoff: canonical agent /root/aws_login_auth in /Users/ryan.porter/Projects/Plexus-auth-login on codex/aws-login-free-auth, based on 03e0b04b67a162c37fbcf3cc9bd28d0c363b571a. Owned scope: official Plexus CLI login, identity, logout, Cognito authorization-code plus PKCE loopback flow, secure credential storage and refresh, dashboard Cognito bearer support, and hosted authorization configuration. Dependency boundary: artifact-store work may consume the client but does not modify it; no artifact ticket resolver or storage migrations in this lane. Behavior specifications will precede production code.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Behavior specification is being tracked in the child story created for the official CLI application authentication flow. Initial investigation confirms the existing client accepts API key or explicit IAM only; the new mode will be explicit bearer auth with no implicit fallback.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Milestone: behavior-first focused Python suite is green (41 tests). Hosted authorization contract is fixed to the pre-registered loopback callback http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback; deployment supplies Cognito domain, client ID, and region. No account-membership claim is required or inferred. Explicit Cognito bearer mode refreshes from the OS keychain and reports plexus login guidance without API-key or AWS SSO fallback.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Risk recorded for follow-up: multi-account membership and account-to-identity mapping are intentionally not part of Wave 1. This login implementation exposes only standard Cognito identity claims and leaves resource/account authorization server-side; a future platform authorization story should define membership semantics before surfacing account selection in the CLI.
